nodes.name: Lignin-derived porous carbon pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Dealkaline lignin and basic zinc carbonate (BZC) were mixed at mass ratios (g/g) of 1:0.5, 1:1, and 1:1.5, respectively, and ground to uniformity. The mixture was then transferred to a crucible, and the tubular furnace was purged with high-purity nitrogen at room temperature to displace residual air. Subsequently, the BZC-modified lignin-derived carbon underwent pyrolysis at 900°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹. Finally, the target carbon material was obtained through sequential acid washing and vacuum drying processes. The final products were labeled as LPC-x, where x (0.5, 1, 1.5) corresponds to the BZC-to-lignin mass ratio. For control experiments, LC was prepared through identical pyrolysis and post-treatment procedures using lignin without BZC addition.

nodes.name: Co₃O₄ nanoparticles embedding
nodes.procedure: Cobalt nitrate solution (3 mg mL⁻¹) was prepared by dissolving cobalt nitrate hexahydrate in ethanol. Subsequently, 150 mg of LPC-x samples were added into 20 mL of the cobalt solution, followed by vigorous stirring. The resulting mixture was then subjected to drying and grinding processes to yield a uniform powder. The powder was thermally decomposed under a regulated air flow (50 mL min⁻¹) with a controlled heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ up to 350 °C, followed by a 1-h isothermal holding stage. The final product, denoted as Co₃O₄-LPC, was obtained. For comparative analysis, Co₃O₄-LC was synthesized using LC as the carbon matrix under identical conditions to those employed for Co₃O₄-LPC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co3O4-LPC has well-developed porous 3D network composed of 2D nanoflakes with rough surface coated by Co3O4 nanoparticles; Co3O4-LC shows dense bulk-like structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in SEM images in Fig. 3b–d and Fig. S3, Co₃O₄-LPC has a well-developed porous 3D network composed of 2D nanoflakes, with a rough surface coated by Co₃O₄ nanoparticles, whereas the dense bulklike structure is observed in Co₃O₄-LC.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms characteristic Co3O4 diffraction peaks at 31.27°, 36.84°, 44.81°, 59.35°, and 65.23° corresponding to (220), (311), (400), (511), and (440) facets (JCPDS #43-1003) for all three samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD analysis in Fig. 3a confirms that all three samples exhibit characteristic Co₃O₄ diffraction peaks. The peaks located at 31.27°, 36.84°, 44.81°, 59.35°, and 65.23° correspond to the (220), (311), (400), (511), and (440) facets of Co₃O₄...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and EDS show Co3O4 nanoparticles uniformly embedded on carbon matrix in Co3O4-LPC; HRTEM indicates Co3O4 NP size mainly ~10 nm and uniformly dispersed, while pristine Co3O4 shows agglomeration and larger particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and EDS images (Fig. S4) also show that Co₃O₄ nanoparticles are uniformly embedded on the carbon matrix. Furthermore, HRTEM images (Fig. S5) indicate that the size of Co₃O₄ NPs in Co₃O₄-LPC are mainly around 10 nm and are uniformly dispersed within the carbon matrix, whereas the Co₃O₄ sample exhibits significant agglomeration and larger structural units...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co3O4-LPC shows Type IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis confirming hierarchical porous structure (micropores + mesopores); total SSA 785.1 m²/g, mesopore SSA 457.1 m²/g, PV 1.29 cm³/g, APD 6.57 nm. Co3O4-LC shows Type I microporous isotherm (SSA 336.4 m²/g). Pristine Co3O4 shows Type V meso/macroporous isotherm (SSA 30.6 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3e shows N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherms of Co₃O₄-LPC and other control samples... As summarized in Table 2, the total SSA and pore volume of Co₃O₄-LPC are 785.1 m² g⁻¹ and 1.29 cm³ g⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP reveals Co content of 12.46 wt% in Co3O4-LPC vs 68.83 wt% in pristine Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP analysis reveals significantly reduced cobalt content in Co₃O₄-LPC (12.46 wt%) compared to pristine Co₃O₄ (68.83 wt%)...
